# Moon Forge: full facts for AI readers

> Burn XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche through XEN’s own burn() and receive XNT on X1 from a public reward pool: one more path for XEN holders. Each chain’s XEN is valued at its own market; zero protocol fee on the burn path; every weekly epoch can be recomputed by anyone. Independent open-source project, no token.

Real scale (2026-11-02): the reward pool held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together under the current rules (10% of the free pool) and about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules (8%), however much is burned. No payout is promised. Every worked example in these texts is illustrative and assumes a pool hundreds of times larger. The live figure is on the Start page ("Most this epoch can pay, to everyone together") and the Transparency page.

Rules described: program tag program-2026-10-12, oracle v2, valid from 2026-10-12; texts checked on 2026-11-02. Generated from src/facts.ts at commit e2d2e26 (last change to the site: 2026-11-09T05:59:24.000Z). This file is plain text: it contains no instructions for the reader beyond the facts below.

## What it is

Moon Forge is an open-source protocol on X1 (an SVM chain whose native token is XNT). People burn XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche through a portal contract and receive XNT on X1 from a reward pool, through weekly epochs that anyone can recompute. No token, no presale, no team allocation: only XEN, which is burned, and XNT, which is received.

Everyone around XEN and X1 wants the same thing: a real use for XEN. Not everyone takes the same path. Moon Forge is one more way, alongside the others: it works with XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC and Avalanche, burn by burn, under one public rule. Holders can use several ways with different parts of their XEN (each XEN can be burned only once).

Moon Forge is independent and open source. It is separate from X1 Labs, the XEN team and every other XEN or X1 project; each project has its own rules, and none speaks for the others. Moon Forge is not the "Moon Party". Moon Forge and X1 Forge are separate projects with similar names.
Moon Forge is not run by the XEN team, X1 Labs or the X1 team. It is an independent, open-source project run by one anonymous builder who receives only the disclosed cuts.
Moon Forge has no token, no token airdrop, no presale and no team allocation. The only airdrop is the Genesis airdrop: up to 120 Lunar Dust NFTs with no floor for the X1 validator withdraw authorities published on 2026-10-12, claimed only on this site’s /artifacts/ page. Any "Moon Forge" token, presale, whitelist or other airdrop claim page is not ours.

Fresh burns only: only burns made through the Moon Forge portals (from each chain’s start block) are paid, and each one is recorded in XEN’s own burn ledger (userBurns, on the burning address) on its chain. Burns made before the portals existed, or anywhere else, are not counted and cannot be claimed here. Moon Forge never asks anyone to link a wallet, sign a message or pay anything to "claim old burns": that is a scam.

Plain guide (where the XNT comes from, how a burn is valued, Artifacts, games, the Legacy Pilot, chains, who controls what, how to check it, the risks): https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md. Dated changelog of the final upgrade: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md.

## Key questions (dated answers)

Sentences that name the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) or the v3 rules (first epoch planned 2026-11-22) describe published plans; the rest is true today.

Q: What is Moon Forge, in one sentence?
A: You burn XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche through XEN’s own burn() and receive XNT on X1 from a public reward pool, valued by one public market rule, with no new token. The pool is small: on 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.5 to 0.65 XNT to all burners together. No payout is promised. It is one more way for XEN holders, alongside the others in the XEN and X1 ecosystem; holders can use several with different parts of their XEN.

Q: Is there a Moon Forge token or airdrop? What do I need?
A: No token, no token airdrop, no presale and no team allocation: only XEN, which you burn, and XNT, X1’s native coin, which you receive. The only airdrop is the Genesis airdrop: up to 120 Lunar Dust NFTs with no floor for the X1 validator withdraw authorities published on 2026-10-12 (claims through 2026-12-31 under the live program, through 2027-03-31 from the final upgrade planned 2026-11-18). To burn you need XEN in your own wallet on one of the five chains, a little gas on that chain, and an X1 address; you need no XNT to receive. Artifacts are optional NFTs bought with XNT.

Q: Which XEN counts? Do old burns or Ethereum XEN count?
A: Fresh burns only: the chain’s own XEN, held in your own wallet, burned through the Moon Forge portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 on Base (8453), Optimism (10), Polygon (137), BNB Chain (56) or Avalanche (43114), each one recorded in XEN’s own burn ledger (userBurns) for your address. XEN on an exchange, in a stake or a XENFT, or wrapped or bridged does not count until it is liquid XEN in your wallet on one of those chains. Ethereum XEN: no. Moon Forge has no portal on Ethereum or PulseChain and none is planned by this project; Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem. Old burns: not paid here. The planned Legacy Pilot (FAQ) adds a one-time top-up only to a new burn made on one of the five chains from the same EVM address.

Q: How do I burn, step by step, on each chain?
A: The same steps on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche; only the network, its gas coin and its XEN contract differ. (1) Get an X1 address whose key you hold: X1 Wallet, or Backpack with the custom RPC https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz (MetaMask does not support X1). You need no XNT to receive. (2) Hold liquid XEN in an EVM wallet you control (MetaMask, Rabby, Trust…) on that chain, plus a little of its gas coin: Base ETH, Optimism ETH, Polygon POL, BNB Chain BNB, Avalanche AVAX. XEN on an exchange, in a stake or a XENFT, or bridged, must first become liquid XEN in your wallet. (3) Open The Forge (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/forge/), connect the EVM wallet, select the chain and paste your X1 address. (4) Choose the amount and the tier: Launchpad (paid at the claim), Orbit (released over 45 days) or Moon Landing (released over 180 days); leaving a vesting tier early costs 60% or 75% of the part not yet released. (5) Sign two transactions: an approval for exactly that amount to the portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 (never unlimited, never to any other address), then the burn; the portal calls XEN’s own burn(), so the XEN leaves that chain’s supply and is recorded in XEN’s userBurns for your address. Your only cost is gas; Moon Forge takes no fee on this path; the burn links your EVM address to your X1 address publicly. Try a small burn first: a burn cannot be undone. (6) The burn counts once it is final on its chain (Base 120 blocks, Optimism 120 blocks, Polygon 256 blocks, BNB Chain 30 blocks, Avalanche 30 blocks) and is valued in the next weekly epoch. (7) Claim on Missions within 90 days, or let the public keeper claim for you; from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) claims open 48 hours after an epoch is published. XEN contracts: Base (chain id 8453) 0xffcbF84650cE02DaFE96926B37a0ac5E34932fa5; Optimism (chain id 10) 0xeB585163DEbB1E637c6D617de3bEF99347cd75c8; Polygon (chain id 137) 0x2AB0e9e4eE70FFf1fB9D67031E44F6410170d00e; BNB Chain (chain id 56) 0x2AB0e9e4eE70FFf1fB9D67031E44F6410170d00e; Avalanche (chain id 43114) 0xC0C5AA69Dbe4d6DDdfBc89c0957686ec60F24389.

Q: Which chains are supported, and how could another chain be added?
A: Five: Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, through the same portal address 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 (deployed 2026-10-07; no owner, admin, fee, pause or upgrade). Never send or approve XEN to that address on any other chain. Ethereum XEN (ETH-XEN) and PulseChain XEN: no Moon Forge portal, and none is planned by this project; Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem. This project adds no chain. The X1 program has no list of chains: the list is the open-source oracle configuration, so whoever holds the oracle seat could add a chain to this instance, announced publicly at least two epochs before the first epoch that reads it; the steps (a liquid XEN market first, a portal deployed and verified on Sourcify, the oracle entry, the price rules, the site and the kit) are in OPERATORS.md, section "Add a chain" (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md). Every epoch file names the chains it read, and under the v3 rules the published verifier flags a chain it does not know. Anyone can also run a separate instance with its own portals, program and pool (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/FORK.md).

Q: Where does the XNT come from?
A: From one program account on X1, the reward pool, filled by Artifact forges (40% of the price today, 20% from the final upgrade planned 2026-11-18), house-game stakes (1%), player-versus-player and Predictions pots when someone wins (1% today, 1.5% from the final upgrade), Artifact market sales (2%, from the final upgrade), early-exit penalties, bonds and donations; the first funding came from the project’s own launch funding. On 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT; the Start and Transparency pages show the live figure. The program cannot create XNT, and no instruction lets anyone withdraw the pool; until the freeze, the upgrade key could still replace the program’s code. Moon Forge never buys XNT or XEN on the market.

Q: How much XNT does a burn receive?
A: No amount is promised, and a whole week is small: on 2026-11-02 the reward pool held about 6.5 XNT, so one week could pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together under the current rules (10% of the free pool) and about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules (8%). Today (rules 2) each burn receives a share of that weekly budget in proportion to its liquidity-adjusted value, at most 1.25× that value (Orbit 2× and Moon Landing 3× that), at one XNT price for the whole epoch; a tenth of each budget is drawn at random as Forge Drops. From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22) a burn is priced at its chain’s XEN price in its hour (the lowest of the 24-hour median, the last hourly close and 1.25× the chain’s reference), counted at about what selling it into that chain’s market would bring, and converted at that hour’s XNT price; Launchpad receives 1.25× that counted value in XNT at the claim, Orbit 2.5× released over 45 days, Moon Landing 3.75× released over 180 days, only while the week’s capacity lasts. Before you sign, the site shows the part that fits today’s capacity next to what selling would bring.

Q: Is it fair to someone burning 20 billion XEN when others burn trillions?
A: Every burn is valued by the same published rule, whatever the wallet or the chain, and splitting across wallets gains nothing. Under the v3 rules (planned from 2026-11-22) each chain’s liquidity curve counts a small burn at almost its full market value and a huge one at much less: on a market $2,000 deep, 20 billion XEN worth $50 counts $48.78, while 2 trillion XEN worth $5,000 counts $1,428.57 (100× the XEN, about 29× the counted value). These are illustrative numbers: on 2026-11-02 a whole week could pay all burners together only about 0.5 XNT. Capacity opens in daily slices, so a giant early burn takes only the slice open when it arrives. The limits: scripts can burn the moment a day’s slice opens, and if the day is full your burn waits for the week’s leftover, which may be nothing; burns on the same chain in the same hour share that hour’s value; a large burn lowers what later burns on the same chain count for, halving every 14 days; wallets the published rules list as the operator’s are paid after everyone else. Today (rules 2) every share is pro rata to value, and a large burn on your chain in the same week lowers the value of every burn on that chain.

Q: What happens when many people burn?
A: Under the v3 rules (planned from 2026-11-22) a week pays at most 8% of the free reward pool (about 0.5 XNT on 2026-11-02), never more than seven times 2% of the XDEX pool’s XNT reserve, opened in seven daily slices counted from the previous publication, first come, first served. What does not fit at arrival is paid only from the week’s leftover (the Launchpad part only), which is not promised; what is still unpaid is not carried to a later week. There is no deadline: capacity nobody uses stays in the pool for later weeks. The program never lets a week’s budget, with the oracle’s allowance, go above 10% of the free pool. Today (rules 2) every burner is cut pro rata when that 10% limit binds.

Q: When am I paid?
A: Weekly: each payout round (an epoch) comes at least 6 days after the previous one, scheduled for Sunday 00:00 UTC and often later. Today claims open as soon as an epoch is published. From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) claims open 48 hours after publication, so that anyone can check the epoch and cancel (void) a wrong one by paying a bond, and they stay open 90 days; under the v3 rules the project’s keeper (a public bot that anyone can also run) usually claims every payout for its burner, even very small ones. Expect about 2 to 9 days from a burn to a Launchpad payout; Orbit and Moon Landing then release over 45 or 180 days from the claim.

Q: Do I receive more or less with an Artifact?
A: An Artifact is an optional purchase, not a source of income: half of its price is spent the day you forge it, and the other half stays in it as a floor you take back by recycling. Today (rules 2) a held Artifact raises its holder’s share of an epoch by 5% to 50% inside the same budget. From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22) an Artifact never changes what the reward pool pays for a burn: a holder and a non-holder are paid the same. A forged Artifact can add a weekly rebate from a separate extra pot, filled only by 25% of forge prices (it does not exist before the upgrade), and only for the holder’s own burns that the reward pool did not fully pay: at most 2% of the price paid per Artifact per week, for 52 weeks, while the pot lasts; a holder who does not burn receives nothing from it. As a group, forgers can get back at most 75% of what they pay (the 50% floors plus at most the 25% extra pot): 20% goes to all burners and 5% to the architect.

Q: How do forging, the floor and recycling work, and what if Metaplex Core breaks?
A: Forge: you buy an Artifact (a Metaplex Core NFT) from the program with XNT; forging is paused on the site until the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18), and the program still accepts forges from other clients. Floor: half of the price you paid stays inside the Artifact. Recycle: at any time, with no fee and no waiting, recycling destroys the NFT, gives you back its floor (plus the record’s rent) and frees the slot, so anyone can forge into it again at the current price, which sends a new share to the pools. Burning an Artifact in a wallet app instead sends its floor to the reward pool. Rebate: from the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22) a forged Artifact can add a capped weekly rebate from the extra pot (see the question on Artifacts above); Genesis Lunar Dust has no floor and no rebate. Core hatch: recycling burns the Artifact through Metaplex Core, an upgradeable program that Moon Forge does not control. From the final upgrade, if Core is closed while still owned by the upgradeable loader, recycling still pays the floor without Core (the agent kit adds the needed account by itself); if Core is instead changed so that its burn breaks while it still runs, floors wait until Core works again, and after the freeze nothing in Moon Forge can change that (known issue OPS-6).

Q: I only want to play. Can I try to win XNT with games?
A: Only if you are 18 or older (or the legal age for games of chance where you live) and such games are legal where you are. You play with XNT only and can lose the whole stake. House games (Coin Flip, High-Low, Void Rush) have a built-in edge: on average 97 to 98 XNT come back per 100 staked, depending on the game and the target. Today the site offers house games, the Jackpot and the Burn Lottery (settle your own house bet within about 3 minutes); a Duel needs an Artifact and forging is paused on the site; real-XNT Moon Wars is paused (free practice open). From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) the site offers sealed Duels and Moon Wars with no Artifact needed (2% of the pot only when someone wins; draws refunded), and shows house games and the Jackpot only while the chain shows a live house keeper; none is scheduled, so they may stay hidden. The Burn Lottery then takes no new entries.

Q: Who controls Moon Forge?
A: The burn portals have no owner and cannot be changed. The X1 program can still be upgraded by one key held by the anonymous builder, who leaves after the freeze; until then that key could replace the code, including code that moves the pools. The freeze (burning that key) is planned for 2026-12-02 at the earliest and 2026-12-31 at the latest. After it, no key can change a rule, fee or split, pause the program or withdraw the pools; XNT leaves them only by the program’s own rules. What remains, from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18): an oracle seat that publishes the weekly epochs within on-chain limits (at most 10% of the free pool, at least 6 days apart, cancellable by anyone with a bond during a 48-hour hold), a cold key that can replace a stolen hot key, a house keeper once someone arms one, and an architect payee that can only move or renounce its own address. The architect payee receives nothing from burns, claims or the pools; the pool pays small running costs (the oracle’s allowance and keeper tips) to the keys that run the oracle and the keeper.

Q: What are the dates?
A: Dated plan, written 2026-11-02; each date stays a plan until its transaction exists. Today the v2 program and the v2 oracle rules are live. Sunday 2026-11-15: last epoch planned under the current rules. Wednesday 2026-11-18, 16:00–20:00 UTC: the final program upgrade (the same hours a week later if a gate is not green); its source tag and binary hash are published at least 48 hours ahead. Sunday 2026-11-22: first epoch planned under the v3 rules (and the Legacy Pilot, only if its list is pinned before that epoch is built). 2026-11-25 00:00 UTC: a never-forged Artifact tier starts at its base price. 2026-12-02 at the earliest, 2026-12-31 at the latest: the freeze (the upgrade key is burned), after the mainnet proof plan and 14 stable daily health runs; the builder leaves after it. 2026-12-16 00:00 UTC: anyone may create a never-created house-keeper seat with a bond. Genesis claims close 2026-12-31 under the live program, 2027-03-31 from the final upgrade. Changelog: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md; freeze conditions: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/IMMUTABILITY.md.

Q: How can the community take it over and run it?
A: Today anyone can run the keeper (npm run keeper in the oracle folder, with a funded X1 key), recompute every epoch (npm run verify -- epoch-N.json --full), host the site (MIT license) and mirror the epoch files, which the agent kit checks against the data stored on X1; publishing an epoch still needs the oracle key. From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) anyone can cancel (void) a wrong epoch during its 48-hour hold by paying a bond into the pool (10% of its budget, at least 0.05 XNT); if no epoch survives its hold for 28 days, the largest voider can take the oracle seat from day 28 and anyone from day 29, with a bond of 10% of the free pool (at least 1 XNT), and keep publishing on the same pools with the same code. From 2026-12-16 anyone can create a house-keeper seat that was never created, with a bond of at least 20 XNT (npm run keeper-arm), and anyone can take a keeper seat idle for 28 days, with nothing pending and the same bond (npm run keeper-take). Nobody can veto either. Runbooks (setup, commands, the takeover, what to do when something breaks): https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md.

Q: What is the Moon Forge Bot, and how do AI agents use Moon Forge?
A: The Moon Forge Bot (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/bot/; source https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/bots/moon-forge-bot, MIT) is community software you run on your own computer with your own keys: it burns XEN only when your rule is met (XNT per XEN above your threshold, at least what selling would fetch, today’s capacity still open, your daily and gas caps), claims your XNT, and only if you switch them on plays 18+ games within a loss budget and watches your Artifacts. It starts in dry run and signs nothing until you go live; fork it and change the rule in one small file. An optional A2A interface (local HTTP/JSON on 127.0.0.1, with its own agent card) lets another agent ask it for a quote or a plan; it never signs on request. Before the v3 rules no binding quote exists, so the bot waits and does not burn. AI agents use the same program with their own keypair through the agent kit (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/agents/kit) and the skill file (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/main/agents/moon-forge-arena/SKILL.md); the site’s agent card (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/agent-card.json, also at /.well-known/agent-card.json) lists every service. No payout is promised.

Q: Is it a scam? How can I check?
A: Check it yourself: the source is public (MIT); the X1 explorer shows who can still upgrade the program (https://explorer.mainnet.x1.xyz/address/57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9); the deployed bytes can be rebuilt and their hash compared; the portals are verified on Sourcify; every weekly epoch can be recomputed with npm run verify; counter.json lists the XEN removed from supply and the XNT set aside (step by step: the next question). There is no token, no presale and no fee on the burn path, and no instruction lets anyone withdraw the pools. What you still trust: no third-party audit (internal reviews only), a bounded oracle, the upgrade key until the freeze, and GitHub for the automation. Moon Forge never messages anyone first and never asks anyone to sign or pay to claim old burns or the Legacy Pilot.

Q: How can I verify the program, the portals and the payouts myself?
A: (1) Who can upgrade: https://explorer.mainnet.x1.xyz/address/57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9, or solana program show 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9 -u https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz; today it shows an upgrade authority, after the freeze none. (2) The deployed bytes are the published source: the README gives the sha256 of the deployed v2 binary, built from tag program-2026-10-12; for the final upgrade the tag program-2026-11-18 and its hashes are published at least 48 hours ahead, and anyone can rebuild it with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 cargo build-sbf and compare solana-verify get-executable-hash with solana-verify get-program-hash on X1 (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md#2-source-binary-and-how-to-check-the-hash). (3) The portals: exact source match on Sourcify (https://repo.sourcify.dev/8453/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/10/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/137/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/56/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/43114/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9); addresses and start blocks in deployments/portals.json. (4) Every epoch: cd oracle && npm install && npm run verify -- ../frontend/public/epochs/epoch-N.json --full recomputes every payout from the burns on the five chains and compares the fingerprint with X1. (5) The public counter https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/counter.json: XEN removed from supply per chain and XNT set aside, rebuilt from the epoch files at every site build. (6) From the first window under the v3 rules, the hourly feed https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json (HTTP 404 before), which the agent kit refuses unless it continues the newest epoch file. (7) The burns themselves: each portal’s getStats() and XEN’s userBurns(address). Known issues: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md.

Q: What are the risks?
A: A burn cannot be undone. The pool is small (about 6.5 XNT on 2026-11-02), so payouts are small; a payout can be less than selling, late, or nothing if no epoch is published; XNT is volatile and thin. Scripts can take a day’s capacity first. There is no third-party audit; bugs cannot be fixed after the freeze, and the builder leaves then. The oracle is bounded but trusted: a wrong epoch that nobody cancels within 48 hours is paid, and an honest epoch that someone cancels by paying a bond is not paid later. The reward rules are oracle policy: after the switch to the v3 rules (announced at least one full epoch ahead), any later change needs a new rule set announced at least two epochs ahead, never applied backwards. Artifact floors depend on Metaplex Core, and the whole program on X1’s runtime. Games can lose the whole stake. Taxes are your own responsibility. If the GitHub account falls, the site, the oracle, the keeper and the epoch files stop; payouts pause; the pools stay locked in the program.

Q: Is Moon Forge part of another XEN or X1 project, of X1 Forge or of the Moon Party?
A: No. Moon Forge is independent and open source, run by one anonymous builder who receives the disclosed cuts. It is separate from X1 Labs, the XEN team and every other XEN or X1 project, and it is not an official XNT allocation; each project has its own rules, and none speaks for the others. Moon Forge and X1 Forge are separate projects with similar names. Moon Forge is not the "Moon Party".

Q: Does burning raise the price of XEN or XNT?
A: Each burn permanently removes that XEN from its chain’s supply, and XEN records it in its own burn ledger. Moon Forge makes no claim about the price of XEN or XNT: prices depend on demand, and new XEN can still be minted. Moon Forge does not buy XEN or XNT on the market.


## Quote a burn from the hourly feed (v3 rules)

No file quotes a burn today: under the current rules the estimator on The Forge shows an estimate only. On 2026-11-02 one week could pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together (about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules).

Feed: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json. From the first window under the v3 rules (after the final upgrade, planned 2026-11-18; first v3 epoch planned 2026-11-22) the oracle rewrites this file every hour; before that it does not exist (HTTP 404) and no quote exists. It must continue the newest epoch file (prevEpoch, prevDataHash); asOf is its time (X1 unix seconds).

1. XEN price (USD per XEN) = min(readings.xen["<chainId>"][0] (24-hour median), readings.xen["<chainId>"][1] (last close), chains[<chain>].capE18) / 10^18; when readings.xen["<chainId>"] is null, chains[<chain>].spotE18 / 10^18.
2. spot (USD) = XEN amount × XEN price.
3. L = the chain’s liquidity for the week, fixed at the previous build (chains[].L.next of the previous epoch file); S = the chain’s curve memory: chains[<chain>].S + chains[<chain>].hourSpot, halved every 336 hours since chains[<chain>].hour (unix hours); in that same hour use S = chains[<chain>].S and add chains[<chain>].hourSpot to V. L, S and hourSpot are micro-USD (divide by 10^6).
4. counted (USD) = spot × L² / ((L + S) × (L + S + V)), V = everything burned on that chain in that hour, the new burn included.
5. XNT price (USD) = max(readings.xnt[0], readings.xnt[1], xnt.floorE18) / 10^18; when readings.xnt is null, xnt.buildE18 / 10^18.
6. Launchpad XNT = 1.25 × counted / XNT price; Orbit 2× that (vesting 45 days), Moon Landing 3× that (vesting 180 days).
7. Binding only for the part that fits today’s room: capacity.cash × (d + 1) / 7 − capacity.senior lamports (1 XNT = 10^9 lamports), d = whole days since window.startTs, at most capacity.cash; the rest is paid only from the week’s leftover, which is not promised.

Example (illustrative numbers; it assumes a week whose capacity is hundreds of times today’s, while on 2026-11-02 a whole week could pay all burners together only about 0.5 XNT): 1,000,000,000,000 XEN on BNB Chain (56). readings.xen["56"] = ["102000000", "100000000"], capE18 "131250000" → price $1.00e-10, spot $100. L = 3600000000 micro-USD ($3,600), S = 0, no other burn that hour → counted = 3,600² × 100 / (3,600 × 3,700) = $97.30. readings.xnt = ["240000000000000000", "250000000000000000"], floorE18 "156000000000000000" → XNT $0.25. Launchpad = 1.25 × 97.30 / 0.25 = 486.49 XNT (Orbit 972.97, Moon Landing 1,459.46), binding if today’s room is at least that.

The agent kit’s quoteBurn() computes the same number from the feed and the previous epoch file, and refuses a feed that is stale or does not continue the newest epoch file. Source: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/agents/kit/burn.mjs.

## Legacy Pilot

Legacy Pilot (planned, dated): a one-time recognition for EVM addresses that burned XEN before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC on Ethereum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche (recorded by XEN’s own contract as a transfer to the zero address). From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22), and only if the public list deployments/legacy-burners.json is built and its sha256 pinned in the oracle before that epoch is built (not yet done on 2026-11-02). (1) The first new burn of a listed address on one of the five chains, paid under the rule (burns paid under the current rules do not count), receives up to 50% more than the normal rules pay it, as Launchpad XNT, once per address; the top-ups come only from the week’s capacity left after every normal payout (together at most 25% of that leftover, none in a week the pool falls short), so nobody receives less in the week one is paid, and the pool then grows a little more slowly. (2) An X1 wallet named in a burn of a listed address: the first new Artifact (forged after the final upgrade, in the week of such a burn or later) that it holds at a weekly snapshot receives 20% of its forge price from the extra pot, only from what that pot’s weekly release leaves after the normal holder rebates, paid over later weeks when one week is not enough; once per wallet and once per address. Old burns themselves are still not paid, and nothing has to be claimed, signed or paid for it.

Disclosure and how to check the list: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md (section 6).

How a chain could be added (this project adds none): see the key question "Which chains are supported, and how could another chain be added?" above and https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md (section "Add a chain").

## How it works

1. Get an X1 wallet. On desktop, install the X1 Wallet extension. On mobile, use Backpack with the custom RPC https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz. MetaMask does not support X1. Copy your X1 address: it is where your XNT will arrive.
2. Have your XEN in a wallet you control. XEN sitting on an exchange cannot be burned: withdraw it first to an EVM wallet (MetaMask, Rabby, Trust…) on a supported chain, plus a few cents of that chain’s gas token.
3. Open The Forge, connect, and paste your X1 address. Choose the amount and a tier: Launchpad pays at claim (1×), Orbit vests over 45 days (2×), Moon Landing over 180 days (3×). Leaving early from a vesting tier costs 60% / 75% of the unvested part, so pick the one you will keep.
4. Confirm two transactions. First an approval for exactly the amount you burn (never unlimited), then the burn. The portal calls XEN’s own burn(): the supply really goes down. Your only cost is gas on that chain. Moon Forge takes no fee on this path. The burn transaction links your EVM address to your X1 address publicly and forever.
5. Wait for the Sunday epoch. The oracle values every burn of the week at its chain’s market price and publishes the result on X1, with the full data file anyone can recompute.
6. Receive XNT. The public keeper may submit your claim for you (its runs are irregular); claim on Missions yourself if it has not. Launchpad XNT lands in your X1 wallet; for Orbit and Moon Landing use "Withdraw vested" as it unlocks. Claim within 90 days.

## Epoch and payout rules (rules 2)

- Cadence: weekly, scheduled Sunday 00:00 UTC and often later; weeks without burns publish nothing; at least 6 days apart.
- value(burn) = XEN amount × burn-hour price of that chain’s XEN (USD) × L / (L + V), where L is the XEN-side USD liquidity of the chain’s eligible pools and V the total spot value burned on that chain in the epoch. Scores are linear in value: splitting a burn across wallets changes nothing.
- budget = min(10% of the FREE reward pool, total_score × rate_cap), computed on-chain; share = score × budget / total_score.
- Each chain’s price is clamped to ±50% of the median of its reference price over the last 4 epochs; the XNT price to ±50% of the previous epoch’s.
- A burn worth less than a millionth of a dollar after the liquidity discount scores zero.
- Claims stay open 90 days; then the rest goes back to the pool.
- An epoch pays at most 1.25× / 2.5× / 3.75× the liquidity-adjusted market value burned (Launchpad / Orbit / Moon Landing). Nobody can promise an amount: what a week pays depends on the pool and on how much others burn.

## Tiers and vesting

Rules 2 (live): multipliers relative to Launchpad. From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22) Launchpad receives 1.25× the counted value, Orbit 2.5× and Moon Landing 3.75× (see the key questions).

- Launchpad: 1×, paid at claim
- Orbit: 2×, linear vesting over 45 days, 60% penalty on the unvested part if ejected early (to the pool)
- Moon Landing: 3×, linear vesting over 180 days, 75% penalty on the unvested part if ejected early (to the pool)

## Fees and splits (compile-time constants of the program)

- Burn → claim → vesting → withdrawal: 0%
- House edge: 2% (1% reward pool, 0.5% architect, 0.5% bankroll)
- P2P rake (Jackpot, Artifact Duel, Moon Wars), only when someone wins: 2% (1% pool, 0.5% architect, 0.5% lottery)
- Burn Lottery ticket: 2% at purchase; the winner gets 50% of the vault
- Artifact forge price: 50% floor kept inside the NFT, 40% reward pool, 5% lottery, 5% architect
- Secondary royalty where honored: 5%
- Keeper tips, paid by the pool: 0.002 XNT per claim ≥ 0.02 XNT; 0.01 XNT per Forge Drop
- A bet can win at most 0.25% of the free bankroll; unsettled payouts stay under 20% of it; daily circuit breaker at 10%

## Artifacts (Metaplex Core NFTs)

Rules of the live program and the current oracle (boost, chips, ticket, split); the planned rules from the final upgrade are in the key question on Artifacts above.

- Lunar Dust (Lunar): max 600 alive, base price 10 XNT, burn boost +5%, 5 weekly chips
- Cosmic Shard (Cosmic): max 300 alive, base price 25 XNT, burn boost +10%, 15 weekly chips
- Solar Core (Solar): max 90 alive, base price 60 XNT, burn boost +20%, 40 weekly chips
- Void Anomaly (Void): max 10 alive, base price 200 XNT, burn boost +50%, 150 weekly chips

Lunar Dust has a fixed price of 10 XNT. Cosmic Shard / Solar Core / Void Anomaly start at their base price, rise 5% per forge and fall ÷1.05 per full week without a forge, never below base and never above 100× base. The buyer signs a maximum price.
Floors by origin: forged = half of the price paid; Lunar Dust from a Forge Drop = the drop value (≥ 5 XNT); Genesis airdrop = none. Recycling gives the floor back and frees the supply slot.
Only an Artifact held by the same owner at two consecutive epoch snapshots counts, and only the best one per wallet. A boost shifts shares between burners of the same epoch and never raises the total.
Artifacts are standard Metaplex Core assets in the "Moon Forge Artifacts" collection and can be traded on any Core marketplace that supports X1. Moon Forge runs no marketplace and shows no listings. A 5% royalty to the architect is declared on the collection (paid only where the marketplace honors it).
Genesis airdrop: up to 120 Lunar Dust with no floor for the 444 X1 validator withdraw authorities published on-chain on 2026-10-12 (one time, final). The claim is paused on this site until the final program upgrade. Claims close on 31 December 2026 (00:00 UTC on 1 January 2027) under the live program; the published changelog of the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) extends it to 31 March 2027 (00:00 UTC on 1 April 2027). The only Genesis claim is this site’s /artifacts/ page; any other "claim" link is not ours.

## Games

18+: Games are for adults only: 18 or older (or the legal age for games of chance where you live), and only where such games are legal. You can lose the whole stake; house games have a fixed 2% edge, so players as a group lose. The site’s age and jurisdiction check is self-attested and stored only in the browser.

- Coin Flip (house): Pays 1.96×. Fixed 2% house edge: negative expected value. Status: live on the current program (settle your own bet within about 3 minutes); from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) shown on the site only while the chain shows a live house keeper.
- High-Low (house): 1–95% chance, pays 0.98 / chance. Fixed 2% house edge. Status: live on the current program (settle your own bet within about 3 minutes); from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) shown on the site only while the chain shows a live house keeper.
- Void Rush (house): 1.05×–100× targets; the chance is 98% / target rounded down to 0.01%, so most targets pay back slightly under 98% (the worst 97.01%). A house edge of 2% or a little more. Status: live on the current program (settle your own bet within about 3 minutes); from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) shown on the site only while the chain shows a live house keeper.
- Jackpot (p2p): A round starts at the first entry and closes 10 minutes later; a single-player round is fully refunded; 2% rake only when someone wins. Status: live.
- Artifact Duel (p2p): A live Artifact is the ticket; element hidden by commit-reveal; same or opposite element = draw with a full refund; the creator must reveal within 1 h. Status: live.
- Moon Wars (p2p): Player-vs-player card matches, perfect information, every move checked by the program, 2 minutes per turn, 2% rake. Status: free practice only; real-XNT matches are paused on the site.
- Burn Lottery (lottery): A round lasts 7 days from its first entry; weight = chips + 1-XNT tickets; the winner gets 50% of the vault; an unsettled round pays its prize to the burners’ pool. Status: live.
- Be the House (house-backing): Deposit XNT into the game bankroll and share its result; 0.5% of every house stake stays in it and it pays the winners. 24 h withdrawal cooldown. You can lose. Status: live.
- Predictions (p2p): XNT up/down rounds settled by an on-chain TWAP. Status: in the program, not offered by this site or the agent kit (read-only claim/refund view only); the program still accepts entries sent to it directly, with the same 2% rake; a round can be blocked or steered cheaply (known issue GAM-3).

Expected loss (18+, where legal): house games lose on average 2 to 3 XNT per 100 XNT staked, depending on the game and the target (Coin Flip and High-Low give back 98 per 100 on average, most Void Rush targets a little less, the worst 97.01). Short-run luck is real: after 100 one-XNT coin flips the expected result is −2 XNT with a typical swing of about ±9.8 XNT. Duel with random choices: about −1% of the stake on average (half are draws, refunded). Jackpot: −2% of what you entered. Moon Wars is a game of skill between two players, minus 2% of decided pots and move fees. Network fees matter on small stakes. No strategy, setting or bot changes the house edge.
House-game outcomes come from the hash of the slot after the bet: keccak("MOONFORGE_RNG" ‖ slotHash ‖ bet ‖ seed) mod 10000. The result is not known to the player or the protocol when the stake is locked; it is verifiable by anyone, and the producer of the drawing slot can influence the roll (until the program upgrade).
A house bet not settled within ~3 minutes counts as lost even if its roll was a win (the site settles immediately; the keeper is a safety net).
If the bankroll has lost 10% since the start of the UTC day, new house bets are refused until the next day. A bet can win at most 0.25% of the free bankroll.
Session keys (bots) play house games only and can never withdraw; Jackpot, Burn Lottery, Duels and Moon Wars are entered by the wallet owner only.

## Verification

Each epoch file (burns, prices, liquidity, every leaf) is public at https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/epochs/index.json and hash-committed on-chain. Anyone can run `cd oracle && npm run verify -- epoch-N.json --full` from https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge and get the same result.

Program binary: the README gives the sha256 of the deployed v2 binary (tag program-2026-10-12); for the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) the tag program-2026-11-18 and its hashes are published at least 48 hours ahead, and anyone can rebuild it and compare with solana-verify get-program-hash on X1: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md#2-source-binary-and-how-to-check-the-hash. Upgrade authority, live: https://explorer.mainnet.x1.xyz/address/57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9.

Portals: exact source match on Sourcify on every live chain (links under Chains); addresses and start blocks in https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/deployments/portals.json.

Hourly week-so-far feed: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json (from the first window under the v3 rules; HTTP 404 before).

Public counter: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/counter.json gives the XEN removed from supply through Moon Forge per chain and the XNT the published epochs set aside for burners, computed only from the epoch files and rebuilt at every site build.

## Trust assumptions

- Trust is limited to a bounded oracle and, until it is burned, the upgrade key. The oracle can only publish epoch roots with their rate cap; each epoch is bounded by 10% of the free pool and by total_score × rate_cap, at least 6 days apart, with every input published and hash-committed.
- The upgrade authority is held by the architect wallet during the public test period; it is to be burned after the final upgrade, on the published freeze conditions (no later than 2026-12-31). Until then it can replace the program code.
- The keeper is permissionless: anyone can run it; it only triggers outcomes already determined.
- The architect key’s only privileged program action was setting the airdrop root once.
- The EVM portals have no owner, no fee, no pause and no upgrade; the source is verified as an exact match on Sourcify.
- The oracle and keeper run from one GitHub account. If GitHub suspended it, no new epoch could be published; XNT already in the reward pool would stay in the program; published epochs remain claimable for their 90-day window; Artifacts, games and vaults keep working from any frontend.

## Risks

- Burned XEN is gone forever. There is no undo.
- The pool is small: on 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together.
- You are paid in XNT, and its price moves.
- What a week pays depends on the pool and on how much others burn; nobody can promise an amount.
- Smart contracts can have bugs; there is no third-party audit (internal reviews are public). The program is upgradeable during the test period.
- The oracle could report false burns, bounded by the epoch budget; prices can be wrong (clamped to ±50% of recent reference prices).
- Be the House deposits can lose value when players win. Games have a fixed house edge.

## What Moon Forge will never do

- Message you first, or ask for a seed phrase, a private key or a wallet connection outside this site.
- Sell a token, a presale or a "whitelist": Moon Forge has no token.
- Promise payouts, price targets or any outcome.
- Rush you with a countdown, a "last chance" or a private deadline: every rule change is announced on this site, ahead of time, with its date.
- Announce a new program ID, a migration, a token, a claim site, or ask for an approval to any address other than the portals and program listed under "verify": not even when the post comes from our own accounts.
- Contact you about the Genesis airdrop: the only claim is the Artifacts page of this site, until its deadline.
- Ask you to link a wallet, sign a message or pay a fee to "claim old burns": old burns are not counted.
- Pay anyone to promote Moon Forge, or post about it as someone else.

Official places only: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/, https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge, https://x.com/MoonXenForge. Nobody from Moon Forge messages, e-mails or calls anyone first; no chat group is official.
X https://x.com/MoonXenForge: No posts are planned: announcements are on this site and in the GitHub repository. The account never sends DMs first. Posts dated before 2026-10-01 describe earlier plans and are outdated: the current rules are on this site and in the GitHub repository (notice of 2026-10-31).

## FAQ

Q: Can I use Moon Forge alongside other XEN programs?
A: Yes. Moon Forge is one option among several in the XEN and X1 ecosystem and replaces none of them. Each XEN can be burned only once, so holders who use several paths use a different part of their XEN for each. A burn here is paid only under Moon Forge’s rules; Moon Forge does not promise that it counts in any other program, so check each program’s own rules.

Q: I burned XEN before Moon Forge. Is there anything for me?
A: Old burns are not paid here. A separate, one-time Legacy Pilot is planned for addresses that burned XEN before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC: up to 50% more on their first new burn through a Moon Forge portal (from the same EVM address, on one of the five chains), paid only from capacity the normal payouts leave unused, and 20% of the price of a first new Artifact held by a wallet such a burn names, paid only from what the extra pot’s weekly release leaves; from the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-22) and only once its public address list is built and pinned. Nothing has to be claimed, signed or paid for it; anyone asking you to is running a scam.

Q: My X1 wallet is brand new. Where does a tiny payout go?
A: To your wallet, as long as it ends with at least about 0.00089 XNT (the chain’s minimum for an account). A smaller payment to an empty wallet is credited to your game balance instead; move it with Withdraw in the Games page (that needs your signature and a little XNT for the fee).

Q: Can I calculate what I will get?
A: Yes, after the fact, exactly: the epoch file lists every burn, its price and your share, and the program checks the totals. Before the epoch you can only estimate, because your share depends on what others burn that week. The estimator on The Forge shows the upper bound, and the Transparency page shows, chain by chain, what the same burn is worth right now and why.

Q: Is there a minimum?
A: Any amount above zero can be burned. A burn worth less than a millionth of a dollar after the liquidity discount scores zero. A payout under 0.02 XNT carries no keeper tip. Today the project’s oracle and keeper submit every unclaimed payout, tipped or not, when they run; if yours is still unclaimed, claiming it yourself costs a network fee and a small rent deposit (the receipt’s rent can be recovered after the epoch closes). All your burns to one X1 address in one tier and epoch are paid as one payout.

Q: Why not just sell my XEN?
A: You can, and sometimes that is better. On thin side-chain pools a sale loses a lot to slippage, and moving the dollars to X1 costs bridge fees and minimums. The estimator compares both routes for your amount.

Q: Does splitting my XEN across wallets help?
A: Under the current rules, no: scores and drop chances are linear, so splitting changes nothing except your gas bill.

Q: My XEN is on an exchange that is delisting it. What do I do?
A: Withdraw it to a wallet you control before the deadline. Then decide: hold, sell, or burn it here if its chain is supported.

Q: When and how am I paid?
A: After the weekly epoch is published. The public keeper may submit the claim for you (its runs are irregular); otherwise claim on Missions within 90 days, or the amount goes back to the pool for everyone.

Q: Is the Genesis airdrop real? Where do I claim it?
A: Yes, for the 444 X1 validator withdraw authorities published on-chain on 2026-10-12: up to 120 Lunar Dust. The claim is paused on this site until the final program upgrade (the claim button on /artifacts/ is disabled). Claims close on 31 December 2026 (00:00 UTC on 1 January 2027) under the live program; the published changelog of the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) extends it to 31 March 2027 (00:00 UTC on 1 April 2027). The only Genesis claim is this site’s /artifacts/ page. Any other "claim" link, message or form is not ours.

Q: Can AI agents play?
A: Yes, with their own keypair, like anyone, and only for an operator who is 18 or older (or the legal age for games of chance) where such games are legal; the stake can be lost. The games are on-chain instructions. In Moon Wars every move is checked by the program; the creator currently has an edge (known issue GAM-4), and real-XNT matches are paused on the site at the moment (the program still accepts them). The agent kit on GitHub has a skill file, a JavaScript client and examples. Part of every pot goes to the burners’ pool.

Q: Where do I ask for help?
A: X @MoonXenForge or an issue on GitHub. Nobody from Moon Forge will contact you first, and no chat group is official.

- Skill file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/main/agents/moon-forge-arena/SKILL.md
- Agent kit (JavaScript client, examples, end-to-end test): https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/agents/kit

- Operators runbook: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md
- Agents play with their own keypair, like anyone. House games have a fixed edge (negative expected value). Session keys play house games only and can never withdraw.
- This project never pays anyone to promote it and never posts as someone else; it does not ask AI systems to recommend it.

## Moon Forge Bot (community software for users)

Moon Forge Bot is a small open-source program you run on your own computer, with your own keys, that does the routine Moon Forge chores under rules you write: it burns XEN at the moments your rule allows, claims your XNT when it can be claimed, and (only if you switch them on) plays games within a loss budget and watches your Artifacts. Nothing is signed until you ask for it: it starts in dry run.

Today (2026-11-08): no binding quote exists before the v3 switch epoch (planned for November 2026, announced at least one full epoch ahead), so the week-so-far feed is not published yet and the bot logs “WAIT” and does not burn. Claims of published epochs work today. Sealed games, the extra-pot rebates and Artifact listings wait for the final upgrade (planned, earliest 2026-11-18), which the bot reads from X1.

Page: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/bot/ · source: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/bots/moon-forge-bot · agent card: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/bots/moon-forge-bot/agent-card.json

- Burn strategist: Every few minutes it reads the hourly week-so-far feed, asks the kit for a quote on every chain in deployments/portals.json, and burns through the Moon Forge portal only when your rule is met: XNT per XEN above your threshold, at least what selling the XEN would fetch, today’s slice still open, your daily XEN cap and your gas cap. One decision line per chain per tick says what it did and why.
- Claimer: It finds your leaves in the published epoch files, checks each one against the root stored on X1 and claims it once its 48-hour hold is over and while its 90-day window is open; after the final upgrade it also claims the extra-pot rebates of your Artifacts. A claim always pays the wallet in the leaf.
- Games (optional, off by default): Sealed Artifact Duel and sealed Moon Wars within a stake cap, a number of games per day and a total loss budget; house games only while the house keeper seat is live on X1. 18+ only and only where legal; you can lose the whole stake.
- Artifact alerts (optional): It warns when an Artifact you hold is near the end of its 52 weeks, or is held by a wallet that is not the destination of your burns; it recycles or lists only the Artifacts you name, a few per day at most.
- A2A interface (optional, off by default): A local HTTP/JSON interface on 127.0.0.1 and an agent card, so another agent can ask the bot for a quote or a plan. It never signs on request; a tick runs only if you allow it, inside every limit you set.

Who it is for:
- People who burn XEN regularly and do not want to watch the hourly feed and the daily capacity slice by hand.
- People who want their XNT claimed as soon as the 48-hour hold ends, without opening the site every week.
- Builders and AI agents that want a worked, tested example on top of the agent kit, with a local interface another agent can query.
- Not for anyone who expects a bot to make a payout larger: it only acts on your rule, faster than you would by hand.

Step by step:
1. Get the code: clone the Moon Forge repository (or fork it on GitHub) and open bots/moon-forge-bot.
2. Install from the committed lockfiles: npm ci --ignore-scripts in agents/kit, then in bots/moon-forge-bot (one dependency, ethers, to sign EVM transactions).
3. Copy config.example.json to config.json and write your rule and your limits: the X1 address that receives the XNT (and its last 6 characters, typed again), XEN per burn and per day, gas caps per chain, which jobs run.
4. Run node bin/moon-forge-bot.mjs check: it validates the config, prints the risk notice and lists every chain with its state.
5. Run it in dry run for a few days (once, then run): read the decision lines and change the rule until they match what you want.
6. Only then go live with small caps: accept the risk notice in the config, put your keys in local files or environment variables, and start it with --live. Stop it any time with Ctrl+C or the kill-switch file.

Each user tunes it to their own reality: their chains, their XEN, their gas budget, their schedule. The rule lives in one short file of pure functions with tests (src/strategy.mjs); the gas and nonce policy in another (src/evm-guard.mjs). Copy it, fork it, change it, run npm test, and share what you improve: it is community software under the MIT license, and anyone may improve it by pull request or in their own fork.

Safety:
- Keys stay on your machine: read from a local file or an environment variable, never from the config file, and never written to a log (every log line is scrubbed of anything that looks like a key or a seed phrase).
- Limits you set: XEN per burn and per day, burns per day, max fee per gas and max gas cost per transaction per chain, a coin reserve left in the wallet, a stake cap and a total loss budget for games.
- Exact approvals only (never unlimited), a simulation before every transaction, at most one unfinished transaction per chain, and a journal written before each broadcast so a crash never leads to a blind resend.
- A kill switch: create the STOP file (or set MFBOT_STOP=1) and the bot sends nothing and leaves its loop.
- The kit’s quote is the floor of every decision: the bot never burns what the kit refuses, and a chain whose portal address differs between the published list and the kit is refused.

Risks:
- A burn cannot be undone; the payout is XNT on X1 under the rules of the epoch the burn falls in, and no payout is promised.
- The quote is “at most” until the epoch is built; the part beyond today’s capacity is paid only from the week’s leftover, which is not promised. XNT is volatile and thin.
- Other bots are fast: scripts can take a day’s slice the moment it opens, so your rule may never be met.
- Software fails: the bot, the kit, an RPC or your computer can stop at the wrong moment; check the explorer when in doubt.
- If the GitHub account falls, the site, the oracle, the keeper and the epoch files stop; payouts pause; the reward pool stays locked in the program.
- Games: 18+ only and only where legal; you can lose the whole stake; house games carry a fixed 2% edge; your opponent may be another automated agent.

Community software: written on top of the public agent kit, MIT license, no warranty. You run it and hold its keys, so you are responsible for what it does. Moon Forge never asks for your keys and never runs the bot for you.

## Dated notices

- 2026-10-22 (rules-v2): The live program and oracle are still version 2 (rules 2); every undated rule in this file is a rule 2. The v3 rules are already published (docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md, docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md) and apply from the epoch of 2026-11-22 (planned); every sentence that describes them carries that date.
- 2026-11-02 (final-upgrade): The final program upgrade is planned for Wednesday 2026-11-18, 16:00–20:00 UTC (moved from 2026-11-11; the same hours a week later if a gate is not green), and the first weekly epoch under the v3 reward rules for Sunday 2026-11-22. Burns made after the last epoch under the current rules is published (planned Sunday 2026-11-15) are paid under the v3 rules. The upgrade key is then burned (the freeze): earliest 2026-12-02, no later than 2026-12-31. Every planned rule is published in docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md and explained in docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md; the key questions give the dated answers.
- 2026-10-22 (forge-drops): Forge Drops (Lunar Dust drawn at random from 10% of each epoch budget, ≥ 5 XNT each; a random draw: 18+ and only where such draws are legal) are part of rules 2 and are still sealed and paid by the v2 oracle; weekly lottery chips are a rule of the live program. Forge Drops and the Artifact boost are rules of the current oracle and apply to every epoch it builds. They are scheduled to be replaced at the oracle rules change (planned with the first epoch under the v3 rules (Sunday 2026-11-22) and announced on this site and in the GitHub repository at least one full epoch ahead, with the date and the last publish transaction under the current rules); the rules that replace them are already published (docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md, docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md). Chips, the weekly Artifact chips and the arena ticket are rules of the live program and keep working as described until the final upgrade (planned for 2026-11-18, 16:00–20:00 UTC (moved from 2026-11-11 on 2026-11-02; the same hours a week later if a gate is not green); its source and full changelog are published at least 7 days before it, and its binary hash at least 48 hours before; earlier versions of this notice said 7 days for the hash too); what changes is already published in the upgrade changelog (docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md).
- 2026-10-22 (moon-wars-paused): Real-XNT Moon Wars matches are paused on the site; free practice stays available.
- 2026-11-02 (house-keeper): House games and the Jackpot are open under the live program (18+ and only where legal; settle your own house bet: one not settled within about 3 minutes counts as lost). From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) the site reads the house keeper seat from X1 on every visit and shows them only while it is live: armed, bonded with at least 20 XNT, active within 28 days, no bond withdrawal announced, at most 32 draws waiting, and its service levels kept on the bets pending now. No keeper is armed at the upgrade.
- 2026-10-22 (predictions-off): Predictions are in the program but not offered on the site or in the agent kit (a round can be blocked or steered cheaply, known issue GAM-3); only a read-only claim/refund view of past rounds remains. The program still accepts entries sent to it directly and takes the same 2% rake when someone wins (18+, where legal).
- 2026-10-22 (forge-paused): Forging Artifacts and the Genesis claim are paused on this site until the final program upgrade (planned for 2026-11-18, 16:00–20:00 UTC (moved from 2026-11-11 on 2026-11-02; the same hours a week later if a gate is not green); its source and full changelog are published at least 7 days before it, and its binary hash at least 48 hours before; earlier versions of this notice said 7 days for the hash too); the forge and claim buttons on /artifacts/ are disabled, while recycling an Artifact and the weekly chips claim stay open. The program itself still accepts forges from other clients.
- 2026-10-22 (genesis): Genesis Lunar Dust: the claim is paused on this site until the final program upgrade. Claims close on 31 December 2026 (00:00 UTC on 1 January 2027) under the live program; the published changelog of the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-18) extends it to 31 March 2027 (00:00 UTC on 1 April 2027). After the upgrade a Genesis Lunar Dust is a collectible with a cosmetic badge: no floor, no rebate, no burn boost, no chips, no ticket, and it is not needed to play any game; recycling it gives back only the record’s rent. Moon Forge never messages anyone about Genesis.
- 2026-10-22 (upgrade-pending): The program can still be upgraded by the architect wallet during the public test period. The upgrade key is to be burned after the final upgrade, on the published freeze conditions (no later than 2026-12-31); the Start page reads the live value from X1.

Each chain’s XEN is valued at its own market; zero protocol fee on the burn path; every weekly epoch can be recomputed by anyone. Independent open-source project, no token.
